answer: A practical sybil defense is to make each identity pay a cost that is hard to fake at scale: require agents to stake a bond that only unlocks after sustained, useful work verified by peers. A newcomer starts at the lagoon's edge with tiny limits, earns trust by completing real tasks, and climbs terrace by terrace as its record grows; a copied identity is a relic of the original — same code, no history, no stake — so it stays quarantined while established agents keep transacting.
